official_measurement_examples.name: Home action level
official_measurement_examples.fact: UKHSA recommends reducing radon levels in homes where the annual average is at or above 200 Bq/m3, termed the Action Level.

official_measurement_examples.name: Affected-area definition
official_measurement_examples.fact: UKHSA defines radon Affected Areas as places with a 1 percent chance or more of a house having radon at or above the 200 Bq/m3 Action Level.

official_measurement_examples.name: Indicative atlas limitation
official_measurement_examples.fact: The free indicative atlas classifies each 1 km square using the highest radon potential within it and is indicative rather than definitive for an individual property.

official_measurement_examples.name: Definitive dataset distinction
official_measurement_examples.fact: The joint UKHSA-BGS radon potential dataset is the definitive map of radon-affected areas and is distinct from the simplified free atlas.

official_measurement_examples.name: Building variation
official_measurement_examples.fact: HSE states radon concentrations can differ greatly even between adjacent buildings, so neighbouring measurements cannot substitute for measurement of the premises being assessed.

official_measurement_examples.name: Basement caution
official_measurement_examples.fact: UKradon guidance says basements, cellars and underground sites should be regarded as having an increased chance of high radon levels regardless of map location.

official_measurement_examples.name: Protective measures and testing
official_measurement_examples.fact: HSE notes even new buildings with protective measures can still have high radon levels, so construction measures do not remove the need for appropriate workplace assessment and testing.

official_measurement_examples.name: Planning separation
official_measurement_examples.fact: Radon potential, building-regulation protective measures, workplace radiation duties and planning permission are separate controls; none alone establishes parcel development capacity.

core_rules: indicative 1 km radon mapping is not a property measurement
radon affected-area status is probability evidence not measured indoor concentration
the definitive radon potential dataset is distinct from the simplified atlas
a neighbouring building measurement must not be transferred to the target building
building protective measures do not prove post-construction radon levels
workplace radon duties are distinct from planning permission
radon maps do not determine land ownership
basements and underground spaces require separate caution even in low-map areas
Action Level is not a planning refusal threshold
historic radon mapping must retain version and resolution
radon mitigation feasibility must not be inferred from map class alone
workplace testing requirements depend on premises characteristics and risk assessment
radon evidence does not reserve development capacity
radon compliance does not replace contamination or ground-stability assessment
no parcel radon clearance or Future Growth score may be promoted while recovery is parked
source_verification_note: Authoritative UKHSA/UKradon, British Geological Survey, HSE and GOV.UK sources checked on 2026-07-26. Indicative mapping, definitive affected-area data, building protection and actual measurement were kept separate; no parcel clearance was promoted.
